answer_text:
# 🦴 Calcium-Containing Foods

Calcium is the most abundant mineral in your body and a major component of your bones and teeth. Since your body can't make calcium on its own, it's essential to consume calcium-rich foods to meet your daily needs.

Calcium is best known for building bones and keeping them healthy, but it also plays many other vital roles — like keeping your heart beating, muscles and nerves functioning, and helping maintain healthy blood pressure.

---

## 🥛 Dairy Products (Highest Sources)

Dairy products (milk, cheese, yogurt, etc.) are the most concentrated food sources of calcium — for example, one cup of milk contains approximately 271 mg of calcium.

| Food | Notes |
|------|-------|
| 🥛 **Milk** | One of the richest calcium sources |
| 🧀 **Cheese** | Parmesan has the most calcium |
| 🫙 **Yogurt** | Also rich in probiotics |

Most cheeses are excellent sources of calcium. Parmesan has the most, with 242 mg — or 24% of the Daily Value — per ounce (28 grams). Softer cheeses tend to have less.

Yogurt is an excellent source of calcium, and many types are also rich in probiotics — a type of beneficial bacteria that can promote immune function, improve heart health, and enhance nutrient absorption.

---

## 🐟 Fish & Seafood

Sardines and canned salmon are loaded with calcium, thanks to their edible bones.

| Food | Notes |
|------|-------|
| 🐟 **Sardines** | Excellent calcium source (with bones) |
| 🐠 **Canned Salmon** | Great non-dairy option |

---

## 🌿 Plant-Based Sources

Tofu is the most concentrated source of non-dairy calcium.

Seeds are tiny nutritional powerhouses, and many are high in calcium, including **poppy, sesame, celery, and chia seeds**.

| Food | Notes |
|------|-------|
| 🫘 **Tofu** | Top non-dairy calcium source |
| 🥦 **Broccoli** | Good plant calcium with high bioavailability |
| 🥬 **Kale & Bok Choy** | Better calcium absorption than spinach |
| 🌱 **Chia & Sesame Seeds** | Also rich in healthy fats |
| 🫘 **Beans & Lentils** | Black beans, cowpeas, etc. |
| 🥜 **Almonds** | Good plant-based option |

Some greens like spinach and chard are higher in oxalic acid, but others like kale, collard greens, and bok choy contain lower amounts, so the calcium they contain is likely better absorbed.

---

## 🥣 Fortified Foods

Fortified foods like **cereals** can make it easier to meet your daily calcium needs. You can also find a variety of plant-based beverages, such as **plant milks and orange juice**, that have been fortified with calcium.

---

## 💡 Tips for Better Calcium Absorption

- **Vitamin D** is crucial for increasing calcium absorption in the body. If you're not getting regular sun exposure, try taking a supplement or consuming foods rich in vitamin D, like milk.
- Certain compounds in plants (e.g., oxalic acid, phytic acid) can decrease calcium absorption. For example, absorption of calcium is only 5% for spinach, whereas it is much higher, at 27%, for milk.
- Your body can't absorb all calcium at once, so it's best to **spread your intake throughout the day**.

---

> ✅ **Daily Requirement:** The Recommended Dietary Allowances for calcium range from **1,000 to 1,200 mg for adults** and from 200 to 1,300 mg for infants, children, and adolescents, depending on age.
